draws.text: Italicise or bold one short phrase where you want emphasis, using asterisks the way reddit markdown does.
draws.else_text: Do not use any asterisks, bold or italics anywhere in this comment.

draws.text: Part of this is easier as a short numbered list. Use one, then go back to prose.
draws.else_text: Do not use a numbered list.

draws.text: Part of this is easier as a few dashed bullet points. Use them, then go back to prose.
Open with a one-line 'TL;DR' summary, then a blank line, then the full explanation.
draws.else_text: Do not open with a summary line.

draws.text: Put a question to the reader somewhere in this, the way you would if you were talking to them.
End with a line beginning 'Edit:' that corrects or clarifies something you actually said above. It must refer to a detail that is really in your comment.
Write this one in the first person.
Hedge one claim in your own words, however you would actually say it. Do not use a stock disclaimer.
Ground one claim in something you have seen or done yourself. Drop it in mid-thought, not as an opening credential.
You do this for a living and you say so, briefly and in passing.
You find some part of this a bit stupid and it shows. Blunt, dry, mild swearing is fine.
Let one sentence end on an exclamation mark.

note: v6's register constraints with the em-dash prohibition and the first-person suppression converted to rate-matched draws, plus the LLM-lexicon blacklist. No structural instruction of any kind: the paragraph campaign was retired after v2 because every generation-side route to matching human paragraph structure pushed the models into an essayistic register that a judge found EASIER to catch (Haiku balanced accuracy 79.2% on the best-matched prompt against 57.3% on phase 1's ordinary one). Whitespace is normalised on the detector side at training time instead.
